title: Acute Severe Aortic Regurgitation Immediately After Cardiopulmonary Bypass Initiation in a Patient With a Bicuspid Aortic Valve.
authors: Takumi Yamamoto; Keisuke Sumii
abstract: Antegrade cardioplegia delivery during cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) is standard practice in cardiac surgery, but it carries a risk of perfusion failure and acute myocardial distension in the presence of aortic regurgitation (AR). In patients with a bicuspid aortic valve (BAV), acute exacerbation of AR can occur immediately after initiating CPB. An 80-year-old man with a bicuspid aortic valve (Sievers classification type 1: L/R fusion), severe aortic stenosis, mild AR, and an ascending aortic aneurysm underwent elective aortic valve replacement and ascending aortic replacement. Immediately after starting CPB and entering ventricular fibrillation (VF), the patient developed sudden, severe AR (vena contracta: 10 mm). This caused rapid left ventricular (LV) dilation and subsequent dislodgement of the LV vent cannula into the left atrium. Real-time transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) promptly identified both the severe AR and the cannula displacement. Following aortic cross-clamping, antegrade cardioplegia failed due to massive regurgitant volume overload into the LV. Prophylactically placed retrograde cardioplegia via the coronary sinus was immediately initiated, successfully achieving rapid cardiac arrest. The planned surgical procedures were completed successfully without further complications, and the patient was discharged in good condition on postoperative day 11. In this patient, the acute exacerbation of AR was likely driven by two key factors: first, a rapid elevation in the transvalvular pressure gradient following CPB onset and VF; and second, the unmasking of latent coaptation failure, stemming from BAV asymmetry and calcification, due to the loss of myocardial tone during VF. Real-time TEE monitoring and prophylactic placement of a retrograde cardioplegia cannula are critical for rapid diagnosis, troubleshooting, and ensuring effective myocardial protection.

title: Lipoprotein(a) Inhibition: Current Evidence, Therapeutic Landscape, and Future Directions.
authors: Pierre Sabouret; Domenico Mario Giamundo; Joanna Popiolek-Kalisz; Luigi Spadafora; Marco Bernardi; Elad Asher; Mamas A Mamas; Dan Atar; Giuseppe Andò
abstract: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is a genetically determined, apolipoprotein B-containing lipoprotein that contributes to cardiovascular risk through atherogenic, proinflammatory, and potentially antifibrinolytic mechanisms. Genetic, epidemiological, and mechanistic evidence supports a causal role for elevated Lp(a) in atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and calcific aortic valve disease. In contrast, associations with other cardiovascular phenotypes are less consistent. Since circulating concentrations are largely inherited and only modestly affected by lifestyle measures and conventional lipid-lowering therapies, Lp(a) represents an important component of residual cardiovascular risk. This review summarizes the structural, genetic, and pathogenic characteristics of Lp(a), examines the strength of evidence across coronary artery disease, ischemic stroke, peripheral artery disease, abdominal aortic aneurysm, calcific aortic valve disease, and heart failure, and discusses measurement, clinical interpretation, and potential biomarkers. The therapeutic landscape has expanded rapidly. Antisense oligonucleotides and small interfering RNA agents substantially suppress hepatic apolipoprotein(a) synthesis, oral small-molecule inhibitors prevent Lp(a) particle assembly, and in vivo gene-editing strategies aim to provide highly durable reductions. Early-phase trials have demonstrated marked lowering of circulating Lp(a); however, most were not designed to assess cardiovascular outcomes, so direct comparisons among agents are limited by differences in study populations, assays, dosing schedules, and follow-up. Ongoing cardiovascular outcome trials will determine whether selective Lp(a) lowering reduces clinical events and which patients are most likely to benefit. Until these results are available, Lp(a) measurement can refine risk stratification and support intensive management of modifiable risk factors, whereas biomarker reduction alone should not be equated with proven clinical benefit.

title: Inflammation After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation: Mechanisms, Risk Stratification, and Therapeutic Implications.
authors: Mihail Celeski; Michele Marchetta; Emanuele Sammartini; Antonio Sorropago; Mattia Basile; Matteo Morello; Carmine Salzillo; Marco Bernardi; Pasquale Mollo; Francisco José Romeo; Arturo Cesaro; Michele Golino
abstract: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) elicits a sterile inflammatory response that is almost universal, yet highly heterogeneous in both magnitude and clinical impact. Initiated by endothelial injury, ischemia-reperfusion, and residual bioprosthetic immunogenicity, peri-procedural inflammation converges on activation of the NOD-like receptor family pyrin domain-containing 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome and downstream interleukin-1β (IL-1β) and IL-6 signaling, leading to increased C-reactive protein levels. This response is further modulated by patient susceptibility, procedural complexity, and device-specific characteristics. While a controlled response promotes tissue repair and healing, exaggerated activation, which manifests as systemic inflammatory response syndrome in up to two-thirds of patients, has been consistently associated with higher mortality, conduction disturbances, new-onset atrial fibrillation, acute kidney injury (AKI), and subclinical leaflet thrombosis. Emerging evidence also implicates gut microbiome-derived metabolites and xenoantigen-driven adaptive immunity as additional contributors to the overall inflammatory burden. Serial biomarker assessment, including C-reactive protein trajectories, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, cancer antigen 125 (CA-125), and novel composite indices such as the neutrophil percentage-to-albumin ratio, combined with multimodality imaging, allows increasingly refined risk stratification. However, no anti-inflammatory therapy is currently established for routine use after TAVI. Colchicine has shown proof-of-concept signals, sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors have demonstrated clinical benefit with pleiotropic anti-inflammatory properties, and lessons from IL-1 and IL-6 inhibition trials in ischemic heart disease provide a translational roadmap. This narrative review synthesizes the epidemiology, mechanisms, clinical consequences, and assessment of peri-TAVI inflammation. Moreover, this review proposes a pragmatic inflammatory subphenotyping framework that integrates baseline risk, procedural exposure, and biomarker kinetics. Such a framework may help bridge the gap between observational associations and precision-based therapeutic strategies, shifting peri-TAVI inflammation from a prognostic marker to a modifiable determinant of outcome.

title: Single-Stage Computed Tomography Angiography, Percutaneous Coronary Intervention, and Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement in an Octogenarian With Femoral Neck Fracture, Non-ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction, and Severe Aortic Stenosis: A Case Report and Literature Review of Multidisciplinary Approaches.
authors: Ming Zhang; Xietian Pan; Lina Yang; Yang Mu; Bo Jiang; Tao Chen; Jing Wang; Lin Wang; Jiayue Li; Jing Liu; Zhuo Zhang; Changfu Liu
abstract: Geriatric femoral neck fractures are associated with high mortality. Early surgery within 48 hours improves survival, whereas delayed arthroplasty is associated with a 41% increase in mortality. Multimorbidity in this population often prolongs preoperative optimization, thereby exacerbating perioperative risk. Current evidence indicates that 5%-10% of patients with hip fractures have concomitant severe aortic stenosis (AS), which independently increases the risk of anesthesia-related complications. Perioperative acute myocardial infarction further increases mortality risk, making cardiac management a critical challenge. The advent of transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) has revolutionized care paradigms. Nonetheless, this situation requires multidisciplinary consensus on optimizing the fracture-to-surgery interval, antithrombotic bridging strategies, and concomitant coronary revascularization. Here, we present a case of single-stage aorta-coronary computed tomography angiography (CTA), percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), and TAVR in an octogenarian with femoral neck fracture, severe AS, and non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI). This pioneering case is accompanied by a systematic review of contemporary management strategies.

title: A Propensity-Matched Analysis of Pre Versus Concomitant Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement With Frailty-Related High-Risk Features.
authors: Avery Love; Duc-Hieu Bui; Shahman Shahab; Avinav Sanjel; Chandler O'Leary; Hani Jneid; Aiham Albaeni
abstract:
Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is frequently performed in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR); however, the optimal timing of PCI remains uncertain, particularly in patients with frailty-related high-risk features. Evidence comparing pre-TAVR versus concomitant PCI strategies in this vulnerable population is limited.
We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX Research Network to identify patients with frailty-related high-risk features undergoing TAVR with either pre-TAVR PCI (3 months to 2 weeks before TAVR) or concomitant PCI (same day as TAVR). Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed using demographics, comorbidities, frailty-related features, and antiplatelet and anticoagulant therapy. The primary outcome was a 90-day composite including all-cause mortality, acute kidney injury, bleeding requiring transfusion, gastrointestinal bleeding, intracranial hemorrhage, acute coronary syndrome, and ischemic stroke. Secondary outcomes included the composite outcome at 30 days and 1 year, as well as individual components.
After propensity score matching, 361 patients were included in each group with adequate baseline balance. The primary 90-day composite outcome occurred in 27.4% of patients undergoing pre-TAVR PCI and 29.4% undergoing concomitant PCI (RR 1.07, 95% CI 0.85-1.35; p=0.56). At 30 days, the composite outcome occurred in 21.9% and 24.4% of patients, respectively (RR 1.11, 95% CI 0.85-1.45; p=0.43). At 1 year, the composite outcome occurred in 37.1% of the pre-TAVR PCI group and 38.5% of the concomitant PCI group (RR 1.04, 95% CI 0.86-1.25; p=0.70). No significant differences were observed in all-cause mortality at any time point.
Among patients with frailty-related high-risk features undergoing TAVR, pre-TAVR PCI and concomitant PCI were associated with similar short- and longer-term clinical outcomes. No significant differences were observed in the 90-day composite outcome or all-cause mortality. These findings support an individualized approach to PCI timing in frail, high-risk patients.

title: Associations of Mild or Trace Valvular Abnormalities With Cardiac Remodeling in Older Adults: The ARIC Study.
authors: Yumin Gao; Jonathan Rubin; Susan Cheng; Lena Mathews; Ajay J Kirtane; Ron C Hoogeveen; Christie M Ballantyne; Elizabeth Selvin; Martin B Leon; Josef Coresh; Scott D Solomon; Amil M Shah; Kunihiro Matsushita
journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
abstract:
The impact of mild/trace valvular abnormalities on cardiac remodeling is not well understood, despite their association with poor cardiovascular outcomes.
Using data from 4684 participants in the ARIC (Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities) Study (2011-2013), aged 66 to 90 years, we examined cross-sectional associations of mild/trace valvular abnormalities (aortic stenosis, aortic regurgitation, and mitral regurgitation) with cardiac parameters using multivariable linear regression models. Cardiac parameters included cardiac structure (eg, left ventricular mass index), systolic function (eg, ejection fraction), diastolic function, and biomarkers (eg, high-sensitivity cardiac troponin T).
The prevalence was 4.3% for mild aortic stenosis, 10.9% for mild/trace aortic regurgitation, and 44.7% for mild/trace mitral regurgitation. Mitral regurgitation showed the most consistent associations with cardiac measures (left ventricular mass index 5.48 g/m2 [95% CI, 4.38-6.57 g/m2]; ejection fraction -1.92% [95% CI, -2.29% to -1.54%]; high-sensitivity cardiac troponin T 0.08 log ng/L [95% CI, 0.05-0.12 log ng/L]). Aortic stenosis was associated with impaired ventricular filling (Ratio of early transmitral flow velocity to early diastolic mitral annular velocity (E/e') lateral ratio 2.00 [95% CI, 1.48-2.53]) and elevated biomarkers (high-sensitivity cardiac troponin T 0.17 ng/L [95% CI, 0.09-0.25 ng/L]), whereas aortic regurgitation was associated with worsened cardiac structure (left ventricular mass index 3.52 [95% CI, 1.76-5.28] g/m2) and systolic dysfunction (ejection fraction -1.54% [95% CI, -2.14% to -0.94%]). A dose-response relationship was also observed between the number of total abnormalities and all cardiac parameters examined.
Mild/trace mitral regurgitation was most consistently associated with all cardiac parameters examined. Aortic stenosis was associated with elevated E/e' lateral ratio and high-sensitivity cardiac troponin T, whereas aortic regurgitation was associated with worsening in cardiac structure and ejection fraction. Our study supports the possibility of pathophysiological contributions of these mild/trace valvular abnormalities.

title: Impact of Continuous Baseline and Discharge Blood Pressure on Outcomes After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation.
authors: Thorald Stolte; Jakob Johannes Reichl; Felix Goetzinger; Max Wagener; Ketina Arslani; Anke von Peter; Rahel Berger; Christoph Kaiser; Michael Böhm; Lucas Lauder; Felix Mahfoud; Thomas Nestelberger
journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
abstract:
Evidence linking pre- and post-transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) blood pressure (BP) with cardiovascular outcomes is scarce. This study investigated the associations of pre- and post-TAVI BP and their changes as a continuous variable with cardiovascular outcomes.
Patients undergoing TAVI at a tertiary university hospital between 2011 and 2025 with office BP available before and after TAVI were included. The primary outcome was a composite of major adverse cardiac events (MACE) at 1 year. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models incorporating restricted cubic splines for continuous variables were fitted.
Among 1191 patients, BP remained relatively stable from pre-TAVI to 1-year follow-up. Both discharge systolic BP and absolute changes therein from pre- to post-TAVI were significantly associated with MACE at 1 year (P<0.001 for both), whereas baseline systolic BP showed no significant association. BP values <115 mm Hg or >143 mm Hg were associated with a higher risk of MACE 1 year after TAVI. A decrease in systolic BP of -5 to -25 mm Hg was also associated with a lower risk of MACE compared with no change.
While BP remains generally stable in the year following TAVI, both very low and high systolic BP at discharge were associated with higher 1-year MACE. Furthermore, moderate decreases in systolic BP from baseline to discharge appear to be protective. These findings highlight the potential prognostic value of BP optimization during TAVI follow-up and support the role of BP measurements as a clinically translatable, independently associated with long-term outcomes after TAVI.

title: Enhanced recovery after surgery turnkey order set for periprocedural care of the patient undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement.
authors: Daniel T Engelman; Gorav Ailawadi; Mark J Russo; Keith B Allen; Pinak B Shah; Molly Szerlip; Adnan K Chhatriwalla; Patrick M Wieruszewski; Subhasis Chatterjee; ERAS Cardiac Working Group∗; ERAS Cardiac Working Group
abstract:
Transcatheter aortic valve replacement is now a leading treatment for severe symptomatic aortic stenosis across the risk spectrum. The choice between transcatheter and surgical aortic valve replacement remains a shared decision, particularly for patients aged 65 to 80 years. Despite extensive device-level randomized evidence and procedural standardization, periprocedural care pathways remain variable across programs. This turnkey order set integrates contemporary guidelines and consensus documents into a practical order set for the periprocedural care of patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement.
Subject matter experts translated existing peer-reviewed society guidelines, expert consensus documents, and randomized trial evidence, identified through a structured PICO-framed (population, intervention, comparator, outcome) literature review, into a sample turnkey order set. Orders derived from consistent Class I or IIa (or equivalent) recommendations across referenced documents appear in the order set in bold type. Orders that were inconsistently Class I or IIa, Class IIb, or supported by peer-reviewed evidence appear in italic type.
Preprocedural care centers on interdisciplinary Heart Team evaluation, frailty and cognition assessment, baseline conduction risk stratification, anemia and iron deficiency screening, structured antithrombotic and endocrine medication management, and weight-based antibiotic prophylaxis. Intraprocedural care prioritizes ultrasound-guided femoral access, procedural sedation when feasible, normothermia, contrast minimization, and balanced procedural anticoagulation. Postprocedural care emphasizes telemetry-guided conduction monitoring, single antiplatelet therapy in patients without an indication for oral anticoagulation, oral anticoagulation alone in those with an existing indication, and early mobilization. Standardized discharge criteria target next-day discharge in appropriately selected transfemoral patients.
Comprehensive periprocedural pathways for transcatheter aortic valve replacement have been demonstrated to shorten length of stay without compromising safety. This turnkey order set translates contemporary guideline recommendations into actionable orders to facilitate standardized adoption of best practices across programs. The composite pathway has not been prospectively validated.

title: Outcomes, survival, mortality, and major adverse events in aortic valve replacement surgeries in Africa: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Victory Bassey Effiom; Victor Oluwafemi Femi-Lawal; Atharv Vivek Oak; Oluwasegun John Oyesola; Fatma Kamal Ahmed; Samuel Ghislain Junior Fodop; Michael James Anayo; Achanga Bill-Smith Anyinkeng; Jonas Paul Ibekwe; Kolawole Victor Olalekan; Samuel Mesfin Girma; Daniel Brabi; Ahmet Kilic
abstract:
Aortic valve replacement (AVR) is the definitive treatment for severe aortic valve disease, yet outcome data from Africa remain scarce. This systematic review and meta-analysis assessed survival, mortality, and major adverse events after AVR across Africa.
Adhering to Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines, we searched PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science for studies reporting AVR outcomes in African populations, covering randomized trials, cohort studies, case series, and case reports. Subgroup analyses were conducted by AVR modality: surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR), minimally invasive surgery (MICS), and transcatheter aortic valve implantation. Study quality was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias tool 2 and the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Outcomes included survival, mortality, echocardiographic improvements, and valve- or procedure-related complications.
Of 2547 studies screened, 21 studies involving 1303 patients across 6 African countries were included; 15 (71.4%) studies were from Egypt. Mean age was 60.4 years; 43.3% were female. Aortic stenosis (70.4%) and regurgitation (64.0%) predominated. Modalities included SAVR (45.1%), minimally invasive surgery (27.8%), and transcatheter aortic valve implantation (27.1%). Technical success rate was high (97.5%-100%). Complications included arrhythmias (16.0%), postoperative bleeding (15.0%), paravalvular leak (5.0%), pacemaker requirement (6.0%), stroke (5.0%), and myocardial infarction (3.0%). Reoperation rate was 4.4%. Thirty-day mortality was 5.0% (95% CI. 3.1%-8.1%), with 1-year and 5-year survival of 93.2% and 91.0%, respectively.
AVR outcomes in Africa show favorable success and survival rate although below optimal benchmarks despite resource constraints. However, results are not generalizable continent-wide, given the heavy geographic skew. Complications including arrhythmias and postoperative bleeding necessitate enhanced perioperative protocols.

title: Human Epididymis Protein 4 in Cardiovascular Disease: A Fibrosis-Driven Mediator of Tissue Remodeling and Inter-Organ Communication.
authors: Shinsuke Hanatani; Masahiro Yamamoto; Fumihiko Ogata; Yuki Okuno; Satoshi Araki; Yuichiro Arima; Eiichiro Yamamoto; Yasuhiro Izumiya; Kenichi Tsujita
abstract: Human epididymis protein 4 (HE4), originally identified as a tumor biomarker, has emerged as a regulator of tissue remodeling, with roles that extend beyond oncology. Recent findings suggest that HE4 is involved in extracellular matrix turnover, immune system modulation, and maintenance of epithelial balance, indicating its complex role in fibrosis and tissue remodeling. In cardiovascular diseases, the circulating HE4 level is consistently associated with disease severity, myocardial fibrosis, and adverse clinical outcomes in conditions such as heart failure, aortic stenosis, and ischemic heart disease, suggesting its role as a marker of fibrosis-driven remodeling in diverse cardiovascular conditions. Mechanistically, HE4 influences fibrosis via protease inhibition, fibroblast activation, and immune signaling pathways, and may function as a mediator of inter-organ communication. In particular, its strong association with renal dysfunction and expression in injured kidney tissues supports its role in cardiorenal interactions. Recent findings suggest that HE4 plays a role in systemic remodeling processes that extend beyond heart function, including those associated with pulmonary vascular disease. Collectively, these insights propose a conceptual framework in which HE4 acts as a context-dependent regulator of tissue remodeling, integrating structural, immune, and inter-organ communication pathways. This perspective positions HE4 as a biomarker and a mechanistically relevant mediator of disease progression, with potential implications for risk stratification and therapeutic targeting in cardiovascular disease.

title: ASXL1- Mutant Clonal Hematopoiesis is Associated with Calcific Aortic Valve Disease and Promotes Valvular Calcification In Vitro.
authors: Aeron M Small; Liying Xue; Shinsuke Itoh; Cesar De Jeronimo Diaz; Yuto Nakamura; Niekbachsh Mohammadnia; Huajun Liao; Yota Maekawa; Linke Li; Sasha A Singh; Taku Kasai; Luisa Weiss; Mesbah Uddin; Art Schuermans; Spencer Flynn; Elby MacKenzie; James C Engert; George Thanassoulis; Peter Libby; Amil M Shah; Christie M Ballantyne; Pradeep Natarajan; Trevor P Fidler; Elena Aikawa; Michael C Honigberg
journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
abstract:
Calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD) is a common valvular heart condition and has no effective medical therapy. Clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP), characterized by the acquisition of somatic mutations in hematopoietic stem cells which provides a selection advantage, has been associated with incident aortic stenosis (AS), particularly when driven by TET2 mutations.
We evaluated the association of CHIP and gene-specific CHIP subtypes with AS in the UK Biobank (UKB) and with aortic valve hemodynamics in the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities (ARIC) study to prioritize gene driver mutations for mechanistic study. We then generated human ASXL1 -mutant THP-1 derived macrophage like cells and evaluated the ability of THP-1 conditioned media to promote a calcific response in human valvular interstitial cells (VICs). We additionally performed mass spectrometry proteomics to characterize the ASXL1- mutant THP-1 macrophage secretome. Therapeutically relevant inflammatory pathways were inhibited with anakinra (interleukin [IL]-1) or tocilizumab (IL-6).
Among 449,109 individuals in the UKB with whole exome sequencing, large CHIP clones and non- DNMT3A CHIP subtypes (e.g., TET2 , ASXL1 , and JAK2 CHIP) were independently associated with risk of incident AS. Among 1,963 individuals in ARIC with CHIP sequencing and echocardiographic data, only ASXL1 CHIP was associated with worse aortic valve hemodynamics. In vitro, ASXL1 -mutant human THP-1-derived macrophage-like cells had increased AIM2 inflammasome activation. THP-1 media promoted VIC calcification, which was accelerated in ASXL1 mutant macrophages. Proteomic profiling identified inflammatory proteins linked to valvular calcification. Accelerated VIC calcification was reduced by IL-1 inhibition by anakinra or IL-6 inhibition by tocilizumab.
Integrating human cohort data with experimental evidence using ASXL1 -mutant human macrophage-like cells and human valve cells, these findings identify ASXL1 -mutant CHIP as a distinct inflammatory subtype associated with valvular calcification and support IL-1 and IL-6 signaling as candidate therapeutic pathways for future investigation in CAVD.

title: Lipoprotein(a)-dependent cardiovascular risk in different populations: are thresholds the same?
authors: Brett S Mansfield; Frederick J Raal; Petri T Kovanen; Alpo Vuorio
abstract:
Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is a genetically determined, independent and causal risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) and aortic stenosis. Large prospective cohort studies together with Mendelian Randomization studies have established its role in cardiovascular risk which has led to the introduction of screening and the development of Lp(a)-lowering therapies. However, interpretation of Lp(a) results in clinical practice remains a challenge, particularly across populations with significantly different baseline levels.
Lp(a) levels vary according to ancestry. People of African ancestry having the highest median Lp(a) levels, followed by people from South Asia, East Asia and Europe, respectively. However, despite these differences, current Lp(a) risk thresholds are derived from populations of predominantly European ancestry and broadly applied across underrepresented population groups.Available evidence from multi-ancestry cohort studies have shown that while proportional risk for ASCVD may be similar across ancestries, the absolute risk associated with specific thresholds may differ. The application of a universal threshold may lead to over-classification of risk in some populations, resulting in unnecessary edicalization and strain on healthcare systems. Conversely, some populations may be under-classified by a universal threshold potentially resulting in avoidable ASCVD events.
This commentary explores the epidemiological, biological and methodological factors underlying variability in Lp(a) levels and their association with ASCVD across populations. We discuss the advantages and limitations of applying ancestry-specific Lp(a) risk thresholds. Lp(a) measurements in clinical practice should be interpreted in within a broader clinical and population context rather than in isolation.

title: Artificial Intelligence Echocardiographic Interpretation in the Emergency Department: Agreement, Interpretation Yield and Reporting Scope.
authors: Vijay Manivel; Michael Hession; Behzad Mirmiran; Patrick Feeny; Nadi Pandithage; Nasim Erfani; Riaz Humayun; Steven Beatty
abstract:
To assess the agreement between artificial intelligence (AI) interpretation and expert emergency physician sonologist review of echocardiograms performed in the Emergency Department (ED).
Retrospective multicentre agreement study in four Australian EDs. A total of 195 echocardiograms (2016-2023) underwent three-stage adjudicated human expert review. Human reports were compared with us2.ai reports. Agreement across 10 validated parameters was reported as percentage exact match with 95% confidence intervals and kappa under two pre-specified tiers: Guideline Compliant (GC; ASE/EACVI multi-view criteria) and Pragmatic (PR; any available measurement). Reference standard reliability was quantified.
Pooled agreement was 76% at both tiers (GC n = 875; PR n = 1323); AI returned an interpretation in 46% of evaluations at GC and 70% at PR. Four structural parameters reached 78%-87%: right atrial size 87% (κ = 0.62), right ventricular (RV) contractility 83% (κ = 0.42), left ventricular (LV) size 83% (κ = 0.52) and RV size 78% (κ = 0.37). Binary LV systolic agreement was 79% GC and 83% PR. Expert reviewers agreed on 85% of interpretations. Pericardial effusion, aortic regurgitation and mitral stenosis, present in 7%-20% of patients, are not reported in the current us2.ai algorithm.
AI agreed with expert review in about three-quarters of evaluations but provided a guideline-compliant interpretation in less than half; a pragmatic approach raised yield to 70% at the same agreement. The AI withheld classifications that experts could reach; its validated scope covers only part of what ED echocardiography must address, and reports did not mark unassessed parameters. This study reports agreement, not accuracy. For now, human expert review of AI reports is required.

title: ST elevation in lead aVR - a marker of critical left main coronary artery stenosis: A series of case reports and literature review.
authors: May Thu Kyaw
abstract:
Lead augmented vector right (aVR) has historically been overlooked in acute coronary syndromes. ST-segment elevation (STE) in lead aVR with diffuse ST depression in multiple leads has emerged as a critical marker for left main coronary artery (LMCA) stenosis and triple-vessel disease (3VD). Recognition of this high-risk electrocardiogram (ECG) pattern is essential for timely diagnosis and improved outcomes.
In this retrospective case series, 5 consecutive patients presented to the emergency department between January 2023 and June 2024 with acute chest pain or cardiac arrest.
All 5 patients exhibited ECG findings of STE in aVR (≥1 mm) with diffuse ST depressions (≥1 mm) in ≥6 leads. All underwent coronary angiography within 24 hours, which confirmed LMCA stenosis (70%-99%; mean STE in aVR: 3.0 mm). A narrative literature review was performed using PubMed/MEDLINE databases (2000-2024) with search terms including "lead aVR," "ST-segment elevation," "left main coronary artery," and "acute coronary syndrome." Literature review shows that STE ≥0.5 mm in aVR with diffuse ST depression has been reported to have a sensitivity of 78% and specificity of 86% for LMCA/triple-vessel disease in prior studies. However, it is important to recognize that this ECG pattern can occur in other conditions, including severe anemia, shock states, and aortic dissection. STE ≥1 mm increases diagnostic yield. Patients with this pattern have higher in-hospital mortality (8.6%-19.4% vs 1.3%) and increased heart failure and reinfarction.
A total of 2 patients underwent coronary artery bypass grafting, 2 underwent percutaneous coronary intervention, and 1 was managed medically.
No in-hospital deaths occurred.
STE in aVR with diffuse ST depression represents a high-risk ECG pattern that should prompt urgent invasive evaluation. Recognition of this high-risk ECG pattern is essential for timely diagnosis of critical LMCA stenosis and improved outcomes. However, findings from this small case series require validation in larger prospective cohorts.

title: Expression of Desmocollin-1 in carotid atherosclerotic plaques and calcific aortic valves.
authors: Kashif Khan; Bin Yu; Sarah Abdulkarim; Adam Schwertani; Jacques Genest; Stella S Daskalopoulou; Adel Schwertani
abstract:
Atherosclerosis and calcific aortic valve stenosis are active, regulated processes sharing features such as lipid infiltration, extracellular matrix deposition, cellular proliferation, and calcification. Their exact mechanisms remain unclear. High-density lipoprotein (HDL) is central to reverse cholesterol transport, and Desmocollin-1 (DSC1) has recently been implicated in HDL biogenesis. This study assessed DSC1 expression and localization in atherosclerotic plaques and calcific aortic valves.
Human carotid artery specimens (19 subjects: plaques and normal tissue) and aortic valves (50 subjects: stenotic calcific and normal) were collected. DSC1 mRNA expression was measured by quantitative RT-PCR, and protein expression was evaluated using immunohistochemistry and Western blot analyses.
DSC1 mRNA and protein were abundantly expressed in carotid plaques and stenotic calcific valves, but not in normal tissues. In calcified valves, DSC1 localized to lipid cores, inflammatory cells, and microvessels. In carotid plaques, DSC1 was mainly found in foam cells and myointimal cells.
DSC1 expression is significantly increased in both atherosclerotic plaques and stenotic calcific valves, suggesting a role in lipid metabolism abnormalities. These findings point to DSC1 as a potential contributor to disease pathogenesis and warrant further targeted investigation.

title: Targeting Lipoprotein(a) in Cardiovascular Disease: Emerging Therapies and Clinical Implications.
authors: Carlo Acierno; Damiano D'Ardes; Andrea Boccatonda; Davide Nilo; Alfredo Mauriello; Vincenzo Russo; Alfredo Caturano
abstract: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is a genetically determined apolipoprotein B-containing lipoprotein independently associated with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) and calcific aortic valve stenosis (CAVS). Circulating Lp(a) concentrations are largely inherited, minimally responsive to lifestyle modification, and not adequately addressed by conventional lipid-lowering pharmacotherapy. Patients with established ASCVD continue to experience recurrent cardiovascular events despite intensive guideline-directed therapy, and this residual risk reflects mechanisms - including persistently elevated Lp(a) - that are not captured by standard low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) management. In this narrative review, current evidence on Lp(a) biology, genetics, and pathophysiology is integrated with a critical appraisal of contemporary management, the emerging Lp(a)-lowering pharmacological landscape, and unresolved clinical implementation challenges. Current management relies on once-in-adulthood Lp(a) measurement for cardiovascular risk stratification, aggressive optimization of modifiable risk factors, and, in highly selected patients, lipoprotein apheresis; no Lp(a)-specific pharmacotherapy is approved by any major regulatory agency. RNA-targeted therapies - antisense oligonucleotides and small interfering RNA agents - and an oral inhibitor of Lp(a) particle assembly have produced pharmacodynamic Lp(a) reductions of 80-95% or more in phase 2 randomized trials. However, topline results from the phase 3 Lp(a)HORIZON trial showed that pelacarsen, despite lowering Lp(a), did not reduce the primary composite cardiovascular endpoint. Full trial data are awaited, while four other phase 3 cardiovascular outcome trials - OCEAN(a)-Outcomes, ACCLAIM-Lp(a), MOVE-Lp(a), and OCEAN(a)-PreEvent - remain ongoing. Should positive outcome data emerge, clinical implementation will require regulatory approval, evidence-based patient selection, standardized treatment thresholds, and equitable access strategies across diverse populations.

title: Prolonging breath-hold duration in radiotherapy using cognitive engagement.
authors: Vincent Huybrechts; Renée De Noyette; Vincent Vakaet; Chris Monten; Wilfried De Neve; Marc Coppens; Liv Veldeman
abstract:
Deep inspiration breath-hold (DIBH) is commonly used in breast cancer radiotherapy to decrease cardiac radiation exposure. Using high-flow nasal oxygen and hyperventilation we achieved voluntary long deep inspiration breath-holds (L-DIBH) exceeding 3 min. Substantial variability in L-DIBH duration among subjects remains, not explained by physical factors. We investigated how cognitive engagement could impact the L-DIBH.
Thirty-six subjects (20 volunteers and 16 patients) each performed 12 L-DIBHs over 4 sessions. During half of the sessions, they were instructed to focus on a mental exercise. Each L-DIBH was preceded by a validated hyperventilation and oxygenation protocol. The baseline DIBH time was calculated by taking the mean of 3 DIBHs. Linear Mixed Models were used to analyse the impact of this exercise on L-DIBH duration.
All 36 subjects completed the four sessions, yielding 432 L-DIBHs, including 216 with mental exercises. The mean L-DIBH duration was 152 s overall and 126 s in the patient subgroup. Volunteers outperformed patients. L-DIBH duration increased both within and between sessions, demonstrating a learning effect. The mental exercise increased mean duration by 14,9 s in the full cohort and by 19,0 s among patients. Its relative benefit compared with the between-session learning effect was greatest in those with poorer baseline DIBH times.
A simple mental exercise effectively increases voluntary L-DIBH duration, providing a particularly meaningful benefit for participants with lower baseline DIBH times.

title: Deep Learning Optimizes the Diagnostic Performance of Coronary Computed Tomography Angiography in Heavily Calcified Coronary Plaques: A Chinese Multicenter Study.
authors: Chunyan Shi; Chengjin Yu; Bin Zhang; Benjamin Ellison; Zhifan Gao; Zhe Fang; Bin Hu; Jiayin Zhang; Ximing Wang; Longjiang Zhang; Heye Zhang; Lei Xu; Rui Wang
abstract:
Accurate evaluation of coronary luminal stenosis using coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) remains significantly impaired in the presence of severe coronary artery calcification. Calcification-related blooming artifacts frequently lead to overestimation of stenosis severity and reduced diagnostic specificity, representing a persistent and unresolved challenge in clinical practice. Thus, this study aimed to develop and validate a self-supervised deep learning (DL) algorithm to improve the diagnostic performance of CCTA for assessing luminal stenosis in patients with heavily calcified coronary plaques (Agatston score >300), using quantitative coronary angiography (QCA) as the reference standard.
This multicenter retrospective study enrolled 786 patients with agatston score (AS) >300 who underwent both CCTA and QCA from four Chinese hospitals. The dataset was randomly divided into a training group (80%, n = 628) for algorithm development and a validation group (20%, n = 158). The diagnostic performance of the DL model and radiologists was compared using sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV) for detecting ≥50% diameter stenosis at the lesion, vessel, and patient levels. Reporting time was also evaluated.
In the validation cohort, 476 calcified lesions in 213 vessels from 93 patients were confirmed by QCA to have ≥50% diameter stenosis. The DL model demonstrated significantly higher specificity than radiologists at both the vessel level (52% vs. 30%) and patient level (74% vs. 57%) (all p < 0.05). In lesions with severe calcification (cross-sectional calcium arc 270°-360°), DL further improved lesion-level specificity and NPV by 27% and 36%, respectively (all p < 0.05). In addition, DL markedly reduced reporting time compared with radiologists (61.9 ± 2.56 s vs. 376.6 ± 127.2 s; p < 0.001).
The proposed self-supervised DL model enables rapid and more accurate assessment of luminal stenosis in the presence of heavily calcified plaques, with improved diagnostic specificity and greater workflow efficiency.

title: Improvements in the Diagnostic Performance of Coronary Computed Tomography Angiography in the Assessment of Heavily Calcified Plaques Using a Novel Deep Learning Model.
authors: Zhonghua Sun

title: DSCrisk: A dual-view and substructure aware based method for drug-drug interaction risk-level prediction enhanced by contrastive learning.
authors: Qingwen Li; Yu Yin
abstract: Combination pharmacotherapy remains a fundamental strategy in contemporary clinical practice. However, the concurrent use of multiple drugs substantially increases the risk of harmful drug-drug interaction events (DDIEs). Developing reliable computational methods for DDIE detection is therefore essential, yet existing approaches still face notable limitations in modelling interaction-relevant chemistry, relational context, and interpretability. In this study, we propose DSCrisk, a deep‑learning framework that employs graph neural networks (GNNs) to encode a dual-view representation comprising molecular graphs and the DDI topology network. DSCrisk further integrates a partner-guided attention readout to highlight interaction-relevant substructures within drug pairs and leverages contrastive learning over DDIE pairs to strengthen representation learning. Experiments show that DSCrisk achieves an accuracy exceeding 95%. Moreover, the partner-guided attention mechanism improves interpretability by revealing critical substructures associated with DDI risk. DSCrisk is available at https://github.com/liqingwen98/DSCrisk.

title: Filtering Out Defects in Open-Source Meat Freshness Datasets: A New Leak-Free Benchmark and a Comparative Analysis of Four Different Mobile Deep Learning Models.
authors: Ahmet Can Citak; Murat Koklu
abstract: Image-based, nondestructive classification of hourly meat-freshness stages is important for food-quality monitoring and supply-chain management. However, detailed audits of open-source datasets and their preprocessed subsets can reveal methodological defects that artificially inflate model performance. In this study, a Mendeley Data dataset for hourly meat-freshness classification was audited at the file and original-image levels. Two major defects were identified: The 36- and 48-h beef classes contained byte-identical images, as verified by MD5 hashes, and offline augmentation performed before data partitioning distributed variants of the same original images across the training, validation, and test sets, causing cross-partition leakage. A leak-free nine-class benchmark containing 1849 verified original images was therefore constructed. The duplicated beef stages were represented as a single 36+ h beef class, whereas the distinct 36 and 48 h mutton stages were retained separately. MobileNetV3-Large, EfficientNet-B0, ShuffleNetV2, and MobileNetV2 were trained using online augmentation, focal loss, inverse-frequency class weights, and five prespecified random seeds. MobileNetV3-Large achieved the highest mean test accuracy (98.51% ± 0.58%) and macro F1 score (98.54% ± 0.55%) and ranked first in four of five runs. However, its advantage over EfficientNet-B0 was not significant in any seed-wise exact McNemar comparison after Holm correction. These findings demonstrate the risks of uncritical reuse of open-source datasets and provide a leakage-controlled, reproducible basis for evaluating compact models intended for mobile and edge deployment.

title: Prototyping and evaluation of a clinical decision support system in long-term care in German nursing homes.
authors: Maximilian Pilz; Anne Gebert; Matthias Brünett; Laura Steffny; Christina Schubert; Jonas Flechsig; Alexander Scherrer
abstract: Demographic change in Germany is increasing the demand for professional long-term care. Given rising requirements and simultaneous staff shortages, the need for digital systems is growing to effectively support nursing staff and mitigate staffing bottlenecks. This article introduces a hybrid clinical decision support system (CDSS) designed to generate actionable intervention recommendations by combining structured data and narrative nursing documentation. The CDSS consists of three interacting components: (1) knowledge models that encode state-of-the-art nursing knowledge, (2) a rule-based expert system that applies these models to generate individualized nursing interventions within the application fields mobility and pain management, and (3) a large language model (LLM) that extracts indicators that are necessary for knowledge-based decision-making from free-text entries to fill documentation gaps. A prototype was implemented and descriptively evaluated in two German nursing homes. Overall, 72% of the CDSS recommendations were rated as "correct" by nursing professionals, meaning appropriate for the care situation. In a separate evaluation, the LLM achieved 76% agreement rate in extracting care-relevant information from narratives. These results suggest that a hybrid architecture integrating expert knowledge, rule-based logic, and language models may have the potential to enhance nursing planning in long-term care settings.

title: Zebrafish behavioral phenomics reveals functional subtypes of autism risk genes.
authors: Karl Stuntzner-Gibson; Ping Zhang; Baixi He; Leonardo Diaz; Yijie Geng
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a highly heterogeneous neurodevelopmental condition caused by many genetic mutations, each conferring modest individual risk. Despite its genetic complexity and clinical burden, no effective treatments targeting core symptoms are available. Although ASD is diagnosed as a single disorder, accumulating evidence suggests that it comprises biologically distinct subtypes, yet how genetic risk maps onto phenotypic substructure remains poorly defined. Here, we apply zebrafish behavioral phenomics to systematically link ASD risk genes to functional behavioral subtypes in vivo. Using an unsupervised deep learning-based behavioral profiling platform, ZeChat, we characterized the behavioral repertoires of zebrafish mutants for 11 high-confidence ASD risk genes. ZeChat analysis revealed distinct behavioral phenotypes for each mutant that was classified into three behavioral subtypes (Clusters 1-3) via hierarchical clustering of their behavioral fingerprints. By integrating mutant phenotypes with a large neuroactive drug phenomics database, we identified subtype-specific correlations with serotonergic, dopaminergic, and opioid receptor-modulating compounds. Using an orthogonal social preference assay, Fishbook, we further demonstrate subtype-specific pharmacological rescue of social deficits, including selective rescue of the Cluster 3 mutants arid1b, adnp, grin2b, pten, and the Cluster 2 mutants pogz and shank3, by μ-opioid receptor antagonists. Together, these results demonstrate a scalable in vivo framework for behavioral phenomics-driven classification of ASD risk genes into functional subtypes and discovery of targeted rescue strategies.

title: Artificial intelligence in human microbiome research: from data integration to explainable translation.
authors: Ikram Khan; Imran Khan; Uzma Noor; Muhammad Irfan; Li Zhiqiang
abstract: The human microbiome is integral to health, metabolism, immunity, and physical protection, with dysbiosis linked to metabolic disorders, autoimmune conditions, and cancer. High-throughput sequencing has generated massive datasets, but analyzing these complex, multidimensional data poses significant challenges. Artificial intelligence (AI), including machine learning, deep learning, and related approaches, offers powerful solutions for data integration, pattern recognition, functional annotation, and predictive modeling. AI applications in microbiome research include identifying microbial biomarkers, predicting disease susceptibility, elucidating microbial interactions, and optimizing personalized interventions. AI also enables integration of microbiome data with host genomics, transcriptomics, and clinical metadata, providing a holistic view of host-microbiome dynamics. Despite advances, challenges such as data heterogeneity, model interpretability, and limited sample sizes remain. This narrative review synthesizes literature from 2015 to 2025 without a formal systematic methodology. We conclude with three priority areas for AI-microbiome translation: improved interpretability, longitudinal modeling, and clinical integration. Leveraging AI in this field holds significant promise for accelerating precision medicine, improving diagnostics, and developing microbiome-targeted therapies, if interpretability and validation challenges are addressed.

title: A fast unknown-input reconstruction solution framework for desired steady-state steering of distributed drive vehicles.
authors: Delei Min; Jianxiao Cao; Yidan Mei; Guodong Yin
abstract: This paper develops a solution framework for fast reconstruction of unknown wheel-end inputs for four-wheel steering distributed drive vehicles, enabling steady-state steering with the desired small turning radius while maintaining the desired vehicle attitude and driving speed. The core contributions of this paper include a novel system constraint analysis method to determine the valid known-variable combinations, a simplified nonlinear tire model for fast computation without accuracy loss, and differentiated iterative solving procedures adapted to different reconstruction problems. Simulations validate rotational speed reconstruction and steering angle reconstruction with output errors of only 1.78% and 3.07%, respectively, with robustness under varying road adhesion coefficients and driving speeds. Compared with model predictive control and deep reinforcement learning, this framework outperforms mainstream path-tracking methods in both accuracy and efficiency.

title: Evaluating imputation methods for longitudinal clinical trajectories: Toxicities in head and neck cancer treatment.
authors: Luuk van der Hoek; Suzanne P M de Vette; Hendrike Neh; Daniel C MacRae; Johannes A Langendijk; Nanna M Sijtsema; Peter M A van Ooijen; Arjen van der Schaaf; Lisanne V van Dijk
journal: Radiotherapy and oncology : journal of the European Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology
abstract:
Longitudinally collected medical data is often afflicted by missingness, making methods mitigating missingness valuable. This study evaluated nine imputation methods for longitudinal data, using toxicity scores measured at multiple timepoints resulting from head and neck cancer treatment with radiotherapy.
For four toxicities (xerostomia, dysphagia, taste alteration, and sticky saliva), toxicity scores at 16 timepoints (1 prior, 7 during, and 8 after treatment) were collected, resulting in 1442 patients with on average ∼11.6 available timepoints. Imputation methods ranged from simple to deep learning-based. Methods were evaluated using a systematic removal strategy enabling comparison of true and imputed values. Patient-level, cohort-level and downstream model evaluation was done, evaluating inclusion criteria for patients, training data requirement and modelling effect respectively.
General imputation quality showed minimal differences between methods, except simple methods, which performed worse. For patient-level evaluation, it was found that when patients had <50% of timepoints available, imputation started to worsen. Cohort-level evaluation showed that advanced methods could reach good performances at low patient counts (150 patients) but were more severely affected by low average timepoint availability. Downstream model evaluation showed negligible differences between methods, other than simple methods which resulted in different model coefficients.
It was found that it is best to avoid simple imputation methods. Furthermore, when applying imputation to longitudinal data practitioners should be conscientious about inclusion of certain patients and if their dataset permits the use of more advanced imputation methods.

title: Knowledge-guided multi-objective deep learning enables robust LIBS analysis for industrial magnesium alloy identification.
authors: Zhenman Gao; Peifeng Liu; Yadong Wei; Bin Tang; Xiaoyong He
abstract: Laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS) has emerged as a promising technique for rapid elemental analysis in industrial manufacturing owing to its capability for real-time, non-contact, and multi-element detection. However, severe spectral noise, matrix effects, and spectral overlap substantially limit the robustness and reliability of conventional LIBS data analysis under complex industrial conditions. To address these challenges, a knowledge-guided multi-objective deep learning framework is proposed for intelligent LIBS-based magnesium alloy identification. The proposed approach integrates hierarchical spectral feature extraction with Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO)-based adaptive hyperparameter optimization while incorporating spectroscopy-informed prior knowledge into the feature learning process to improve interpretability and generalization. Unlike conventional optimization strategies that focus solely on classification accuracy, the proposed framework simultaneously optimizes classification accuracy, noise robustness, and computational efficiency. Extensive experiments, including multi-level noise evaluation, ablation analysis, Grad-CAM visualization, inference latency measurement, and stratified five-fold cross-validation, demonstrate the superiority of the proposed method. The optimized model achieves an average classification accuracy of 99.90%, exhibits exceptional robustness under severe spectral interference, and reaches saturated performance within 150 training epochs under a maximum training setting of 200 epochs with early-stopping strategy, and maintains an inference latency of approximately 45 ms. Furthermore, the extremely low cross-validation standard deviation (0.0002) confirms excellent model stability and generalization across different data partitions. These results demonstrate that the proposed strategy provides a robust, interpretable, and practically deployable solution for intelligent LIBS analysis in industrial material identification.

title: Research progress on the mechanism and clinical significance of immunoediting in the malignant transformation of oral leukoplakia.
authors: Jinyu Wang; Yu Ma; Jiayu Ren; Ruoming Wang; Yajun Wang; Mengyuan Yang; Yingjie Jia; Jiawei Chai; Wenmin Xing; Yahui Wang; Fang Zhang
abstract: The insidious malignant transformation of oral leukoplakia (OLK) into oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) represents a critical clinical bottleneck in head and neck oncology. Grounded in the cancer immunoediting theory of "elimination-equilibrium-escape," this review systematically reconstructs the spatiotemporal continuum of OLK transitioning toward malignant conversion. We comprehensively dissect the localized immunosuppressive network centered on T cell exhaustion, Natural killer cell inactivation, M2 macrophage polarization, antigen-presenting cell defects, and the dual roles of fibroblasts, elucidating the interactive mechanisms that drive mucosal barrier collapse and immune escape. Accordingly, this paper focuses on the translational pathways of leveraging multimodal deep learning algorithms and big data oncology to integrate heterogeneous omics data, thereby constructing chairside precision decision-making systems. This review ultimately aims to offer a new perspective on the clinical management of oral premalignant lesions, rendering the transition from traditional "reactive surveillance" to algorithm-driven "precision cancer interception" clinically feasible.

title: Accelerating training speed of tiny recursive models with curriculum guided adaptive recursion.
authors: Kaleem Ullah Qasim; Jiashu Zhang; Razan Alharith; Muhammad Kafeel Shaheen
journal: Neural networks : the official journal of the International Neural Network Society
abstract: Recursive reasoning models solve complex reasoning tasks through iterative refinement, enabling tiny networks to rival far larger language models. However, training remains expensive: prior work reports 36 GPU-hours for Sudoku-Extreme. We propose CGAR, a training methodology that applies curriculum learning to architectural depth rather than data ordering. CGAR combines Progressive Depth Curriculum (PDC), which adjusts recursion depth from shallow to deep configurations during training, and Hierarchical Supervision Weighting (HSW), which applies exponentially decaying importance to supervision steps to align loss weighting with observed gradient magnitude decay. On Sudoku-Extreme (423,168 test puzzles), CGAR achieves 1.71 ×  training speedup (10.93 to 6.38 hours, 42% cost reduction) with only 0.63% accuracy drop (86.65% to 86.02%), while preventing late-stage overfitting that degrades baseline to 86.31%. Ablations reveal PDC alone achieves 2.26 ×  speedup at 85.47% accuracy, improving training efficiency and accuracy at once. The speedup reproduces on Maze-Hard and ARC-AGI-1 (1.25-1.71 ×  over three tasks), with the fixed-depth baseline failing to learn ARC-AGI-1 under matched budget. CGAR-trained models exhibit near-perfect halting accuracy (99.5% for full CGAR; 100% for the PDC-only configuration) and 6% fewer reasoning steps. Curriculum on architectural depth enables efficient training of recursive reasoners on modest hardware. Code: https://github.com/Kaleemullahqasim/CGAR.

title: Integrating deep learning and radiomics for accurate differentiation of benign and malignant breast microcalcifications on intraoperative specimen mammography.
authors: Shengying Chen; Wanwei Jian; Zheng Li; Jiafa He; Geng Yang; Lingling Ye; Xue Song; Xiaojie Lin; Chang Qiu; Qianqian Guo; Yan Dai; Xuetao Wang; Rui Xu
journal: Applied radiation and isotopes : including data, instrumentation and methods for use in agriculture, industry and medicine
abstract:
Mammography (MG) remains the cornerstone imaging modality for early breast cancer screening, playing a pivotal role in lowering disease-specific mortality. Nevertheless, its diagnostic utility is constrained by a substantial false-negative rate, documented between 10% and 30%. This limitation poses significant clinical challenges in evaluating suspicious microcalcifications on surgical excision biopsy. Intraoperative frozen section analysis often yields inconclusive findings for such calcified lesions, potentially necessitating re-operation. Consequently, rigorous assessment of mammographic features in excised specimens is essential for optimizing surgical decision-making, particularly regarding the necessity and timing of intraoperative pathological evaluation.
This investigation involved a retrospective evaluation of 400 intraoperative specimen mammography obtained from individuals confirmed to have breast cancer at the Guangdong Provincial Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine. We herein focus exclusively on intraoperative specimen mammography, which is distinct from conventional screening mammography. Upon securing necessary ethical clearance, we assembled a rigorously screened dataset comprising 197 benign and 203 malignant instances. Prior to analysis, images were subjected to preprocessing steps such as grayscale transformation and histogram equalization to optimize them for deep learning ingestion. We subsequently constructed the EfficientNet_radiomics framework by fusing latent representations from the EfficientNet-B0 architecture with manually engineered radiomic descriptors extracted from the imaging data, a strategy designed to augment the system's diagnostic precision.
Compared with conventional machine learning approaches and experienced radiologists, our framework yielded superior diagnostic metrics. Notably, it achieved 78.0% ± 7.0 accuracy in identifying benign calcifications versus 71.4% ± 8.0 for radiologists, and 83.0% ± 6.0 versus 81.8% ± 6.0 for malignant lesions, underscoring its translational value for clinical deployment.
The study holds promise as a real-time decision-support tool during intraoperative specimen evaluation, potentially reducing unnecessary frozen section analyses and re-operation rates by providing more accurate intraoperative differentiation, particularly for benign calcifications.

title: MRI-derived radiomics for prostate cancer active surveillance: a systematic review.
authors: Eimear T Kyle; Kevin J Sweeney; Devin H McCabe; Niall J O'Sullivan; Alison Corr; Niall Sheehy; James Meaney; Peter Lonergan; Louise C McLoughlin; Michael E Kelly
abstract:
To systematically review MRI-derived radiomic and artificial intelligence models predicting outcomes in men on or eligible for active surveillance (AS) for prostate cancer, and whether reported endpoints permit quantitative synthesis.
Following PRISMA 2020, we searched PubMed, Scopus, Embase, and Web of Science (2000-September 2026). Two reviewers independently screened, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias (QUADAS-2, PROBAST) and methodological quality (METRICS). Three subgroups were defined: AS selection at diagnosis, baseline detection of clinically significant cancer, and progression during follow-up. Pooling was pre-specified for subgroups with at least four independent cohorts; endpoint equivalence was assessed.
Seventeen studies across 12 unique cohorts were included. Seven publications derived from two cohorts; 12 independent cohort-level estimates (n = 2703) remained after overlap resolution. Nine publications (four independent cohorts) addressed progression (AUC 0.70 to 0.95), but progression was defined in five non-equivalent ways, from any grade-group increase to composite core-count criteria, precluding quantitative synthesis. Risk of bias was high or unclear in 16 of 17 studies; the median METRICS score was 32.3 % (range 18.9-52.3 %). No study reported external validation or calibration for progression.
Progression endpoints were heterogeneous and several were of limited clinical relevance. A core outcome set for AS (at least ISUP grade group ≥3 and/or unequivocal radiological progression), followed by multi-centre external validation with a head-to-head comparison against the PRECISE v2 (Prostate Cancer Radiological Estimation of Change in Sequential Evaluation) score, is the priority before clinical use can be considered.

title: Time-resolved monitoring of key tea fermentation indicators via Raman-NIR spectroscopic fusion and deep learning-based predictive modeling.
authors: Min Liu; Renyong Cao; Nama Yaa Akyea Prempeh; Jie Jiang; Jiali Ji; Daokun Wang; Wanping Fang
abstract: Routine monitoring of black tea fermentation relies on destructive and time-consuming wet chemistry methods. Therefore, a non-destructive analytical strategy combining Raman and near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy with deep learning was developed for simultaneously monitoring key fermentation indicators. Fresh Camellia sinensis leaves were fermented for 4 h under controlled temperature and humidity, with samples collected at nine time points. Concentrations of total tea polyphenols, theabrownins, and theaflavins were determined using standard reference methods, while corresponding Raman spectra (400-2500 cm-1) and NIR spectra (970-1700 nm) were acquired. The spectral data were integrated via low-level fusion and subsequently modeled using convolutional neural networks (CNN) and long short-term memory (LSTM) networks. The fused LSTM model yielded the best predictive performance, with Rp values of 0.9395, 0.9345, and 0.8596 for total tea polyphenols, theabrownins, and theaflavins, respectively. These results demonstrate the potential of Raman-NIR spectral fusion combined with deep learning for non-destructive testing of key quality indicators during black tea fermentation.

title: A frequency-driven method for retinal vessel segmentation.
authors: Haoren Xiong; Fei Long; Hang Hu; You Li; Shanjun Zhang; Jun Sang
journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
abstract:
Retinal vessel segmentation is essential for diagnosing and monitoring ocular and systemic diseases. However, most existing deep learning methods operate predominantly in the spatial domain, limiting their ability to capture fine vessel structures and maintain topological continuity, especially for thin and low-contrast vessels. Existing frequency-aware approaches mostly rely on fixed transforms or simple feature concatenation, lacking task-adaptive spectral modeling. We developed a frequency-driven framework to address these limitations.
We implemented FRetinalNet, a frequency-driven encoder-decoder architecture. The encoder employs a Frequency Feature Tuning Block (FFTBlock) that parameterizes convolutional kernels in the spectral domain and adaptively modulates them with contextual cues via inverse FFT. Spatial and frequency features from parallel branches are fused using a Frequency Aware Fusion Block (FaFBlock) with cross-modality attention. The decoder includes dual-resolution branches for fine boundary recovery and global structural coherence, along with an auxiliary decoder for complementary supervision. Training proceeds in two stages: Stage 1 pretrains the encoder with original and Dual-Tree Complex Wavelet Transform inputs using consistency loss; Stage 2 transfers weights and fine-tunes under supervised objectives. We evaluated on DRIVE, STARE, and OCTA-500 using Dice, sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and AUC.
FRetinalNet achieved the highest Dice scores on DRIVE (0.8578) and STARE (0.8696) compared with state-of-the-art methods. On OCTA-500, it obtained the best Dice for arteries (0.8864) and veins (0.9055) on the 6mm subset, and the best arterial (0.9169) and venous (0.9101) Dice on the 3mm subset. Ablation studies confirmed that two-stage training improves Dice from 0.8390 to 0.8578, and that all proposed components provide complementary benefits.
Explicit integration of learnable spectral parameterization and cross-domain feature fusion improves delineation of fine structures and topological continuity. The two-stage training pipeline provides robust frequency-aware initialization across fundus and OCTA modalities.

title: Differentiable End-to-End Sensor Array Optimization for Electronic Nose via Local Self-Attention.
authors: Zhiyuan Qu; Chen Su; Lu Zhang; Tao Du; Xiyang Liu; Weiwei Wu; Taoping Liu
abstract: Electronic noses (e-noses) based on cross-selective gas sensors often suffer from severe redundancy, which degrades odor analysis accuracy and impedes practical deployment. Here, we introduce a fully deep-learning-based sensor array optimization (SAO) framework that learns an optimal subset of sensor array through an end-to-end differentiable manner. Unlike conventional step-by-step workflows, which separate feature extraction, feature selection, sensor selection, and model training, our method jointly optimizes the sensor selection strategy, feature extractor, and task-specific network, enabling global collaborative optimization. Core to the framework is a local self-attention mechanism that infers sensor-wise importance while preserving the temporal structure of individual sensor responses, together with a tanhshrink-based gating function that drives redundant channels exactly to zero without requiring explicit sparsity regularization. Experiments on a 13-channel polyaniline sensor array exposed to six volatile organic compounds show that the proposed method achieves an accuracy of 91.18 ± 0.55% using only four sensors, reducing the number of sensors by nearly 70% while outperforming conventional approaches. These results demonstrate that the differentiable SAO can improve both efficiency and accuracy in practical e-nose applications.

title: Dermoscopy-Based AI Risk Scoring Enhanced Experienced Dermatologists' Decision-Making: a Large Retrospective Reader Study.
authors: Laudine Janssen; Sofie Van Kelst; Heleen Cokelaere; Julie Terrasson; Julie De Smedt; Alexandre Bohyn; Bart Diricx; Jonas De Vylder; Tom Kimpe; Jorien Papeleu; Evelien Verhaeghe; Lieve Brochez; Marjan Garmyn
abstract:
The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in dermoscopy is promising for diagnostic and management decisions.
This study aimed to assess the impact of a deep learning-generated AI risk score, based on dermoscopic images and metadata, on dermatologists' diagnostic accuracy, confidence, and management strategy for lesions suspicious of skin cancer.
A neural network was developed using a database of dermoscopic images of benign and malignant skin lesions, including both proprietary and public data. In a multicenter, cross-sectional study, 104 experienced dermatologists, with a median dermoscopic experience of 10 years, evaluated batches from a test set of 922 skin lesions, including 577 benign (63%) and 345 malignant (37%) cases, resulting in a dataset comprising 9,198 observations. Each case was assessed before and after the AI-generated risk score. Key outcomes included accurate diagnosis, correct decision on malignancy, and management strategy.
Overall accuracy for correct diagnosis increased from 74.6% before AI to 81.6% after AI (95% confidence interval (CI): 3.8%-10.2%; P<0.001). Overall sensitivity for decision on malignancy increased from 91.7% before AI, to 97.6% after AI (95% CI: 2.9%-8.8%; P<0.001). The biggest increase in sensitivity was seen for melanoma and high-grade dysplastic naevi, from 79.0% before AI to 93.8% after AI (95% CI: 5.4%-24.4%; P=0.002). AI was significantly associated with choosing the correct management strategy (53.5% to 59.0%, 95% CI: 2.5%-8.5%; P<0.001).
AI enhanced experienced dermatologists' decision-making, particularly for melanoma and high-grade dysplastic naevi. Future prospective studies should further explore AI's integration into routine clinical settings.

title: Machine Learning for Predicting Dental Caries Presence and Severity: An Age-Cohort Perspective from a Nationally Representative Survey in Brazil.
authors: Jessye Melgarejo do Amaral Giordani; Orlando Luiz do Amaral Júnior; Maria Laura Braccini Fagundes; Juliana Balbinot Hilgert; Fernando Neves Hugo
abstract:
Although preventable, dental caries remains a global public health challenge due to its multifactorial nature and the deep influence of socio-structural determinants. This study evaluates the performance of Artificial Intelligence (AI) models as decision-support frameworks for population-level risk stratification, screening, and public health planning.
We analyzed a representative sample (N=23,726) from the SB Brasil 2023 national survey, stratified into three age cohorts: children (12y), adolescents (15-19y), and adults (35-44y). Eleven predictors, encompassing socioeconomic (wealth score via PCA, household density, race, water access), psychosocial (self-rated oral health status), behavioral, and clinical domains, were used to predict caries presence (classification: D>=1) and severity (DMFT index regression). To account for overdispersion and the high frequency of zero counts, we utilized advanced count-based regressions, including Zero-Inflated Negative Binomial (ZINB) and Negative Binomial (NB) models. Performance was assessed using AUC, Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and Decision Curve Analysis (DCA) via 5-fold cross-validation.
Caries prevalence increased progressively with age (36.8% to 52.7%). The non-clinical triage models demonstrated significant Net Benefit in DCA across all groups, effectively identifying high-risk individuals for prioritization without requiring clinical examination. For severity prediction, the ZINB model identified structural signals of inequity, particularly in late adolescence (15-19y), where socio-structural determinants explained a meaningful proportion of clinical variance (R2=0.1010; MAE=2.79). Across all stages, SHAP analysis reinforced that wealth score and household density are the primary structural predictors of caries risk.
AI provides a feasible framework for population-level risk stratification and public health planning. The findings suggest that AI-driven frameworks should be utilized for managerial triage and resource allocation, enabling proportional universalism by identifying high-risk clusters through structural determinants rather than individual-level clinical diagnostics.

title: Patient-Specific Analysis of Ventricular Vortex Formation and Flow Energetics in Rheumatic and Calcific Mitral Stenosis
authors: Marshall Davey; Mohammad Saber Hashemi; Gregg S. Pressman; Arash Kheradvar; Boyce E. Griffith
abstract: Abstract                                        Purpose                                            Mitral stenosis (MS) accounts for 12% of cardiac patients with single valve disease. There are two main causes: rheumatic disease of the mitral valve (MV) and mitral annular calcification (MAC). While both result in increased transmitral pressure gradients, each has unique effects on valve morphology and pathophysiology. We aimed to study differences in transmitral vortex formation and stroke energetics between the two valve types. We created an                       in silico                       experimental system using an immersed finite element-finite difference fluid-structure interaction (FSI) scheme and performed three-dimensional flow field analysis.                                                                                Materials and Methods                     Patient-specific, echocardiographic-derived geometries from a healthy MV, a MAC-associated MS valve, and a rheumatic disease-associated MS (RMS) valve were translated into finite element meshes and situated within a left ventricle model driven by a pump-approximating pressure boundary condition at 70 bpm and cardiac outputs of 1.5, 3, 3.5, and 5 L/min over eight cycles.                                                           Results                     RMS had smaller geometric and effective orifice areas than MAC, but the RMS–MAC differences in mean transmitral pressure gradient and peak transmitral velocity depended on cardiac output. Across equivalent cardiac output conditions, the MAC case required greater pump stroke work and exhibited higher three-dimensional ventricular kinetic energy and viscous energy dissipation than the RMS case. Both diseased cases showed disrupted mitral vortex formation.                                                           Conclusion                     Three-dimensional FSI simulations suggest that MAC-associated MS may impose a greater energetic burden on ventricular flow than RMS, revealing etiology-specific hemodynamic signatures and providing potential mechanistic insight for improved characterization of MS, warranting further investigation with an expanded valve cohort.

authors: Katane Elizabeth Kekana; Thokozani Isaac Mtshali
journal: Journal of Education and Learning Technology
abstract: Teaching learners with special educational needs requires dynamic and adaptive pedagogical strategies that can lead to social development and academic success. This can be possible if teachers are assisted in mitigating the daily challenges of teaching such learners. This qualitative exploratory case study investigated the pedagogical challenges encountered by two Grade 9 Technology teachers in the Capricorn District of Limpopo Province. This study used Shulman’s Content and Pedagogical Knowledge framework to understand teachers’ challenges. Data was collected through semi-structured interviews and classroom observations; all collected data were analysed thematically. This study found that teachers experienced various challenges, including the emotional labour of teaching, burnout in the LSEN environment and the enactment of instructional knowledge. The study concluded that the sampled teachers displayed weaknesses in lesson planning, activating learners’ prior knowledge, diagnosing errors, achieving curriculum objectives and sustaining engagement. As a result, it was recommended that support through teacher assistants, creative differentiated strategies and enhanced digital-technology literacy to improve outcomes for learners with special needs was imminent.

title: Integration of Biomechanics and Digital Technology: Using Kinovea for Motion Analysis and Learning for Beginner Athletes
authors: Muhammad Nur Hudha; Riezky Maya Probosari; Annisa Nur Khasanah; Supurwoko; Salsabila Kholifahtun Nisa’; Gifran Rihla Gifarka Latief
journal: Journal of Coaching and Sports Science
abstract: Background: The integration of biomechanics with digital motion-analysis technologies has introduced new approaches for examining movement efficiency, kinematic characteristics, and technical patterns in walking and running activities. Kinovea, as an accessible motion-analysis software, provides both visual and quantitative feedback. However, its application in supporting technique development among beginner athletes remains insufficiently explored. Aim: This study aims to describe the use of Kinovea in biomechanics training and examine its contribution to the awareness of kinematic characteristics and movement techniques among beginner athletes. Methods: A descriptive qualitative design involved 72 beginner athletes aged 18–25 years selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected over 16 weeks through interviews, field observations, and motion video recordings analyzed using Kinovea. Kinematic data focused on joint angles, stride behavior, and movement phases during walking, running, and the flight phase. Qualitative data were analyzed using content analysis with NVivo 12, while kinematic results were interpreted descriptively to identify performance patterns and areas for technical refinement. Result: Kinematic analysis showed coordinated joint-angle patterns across all phases. Walking analysis identified arm swing angles of 50.9°–58.8° and leg separation angles of 64.3°–67.2°, indicating a stable gait rhythm. The running analysis revealed knee angles of 68.8°–69.8° and elbow angles of 87.6°–89.1°, indicating efficient propulsive mechanics. The flight phase demonstrated knee angles of 81.2°–87.8° and elbow angles of 80.4°–88.3°, suggesting effective momentum use and postural stability. These measurements supported stride-efficiency assessment and technique evaluation. Qualitative findings revealed that Kinovea enabled athletes to interpret movement phases and identify technical inefficiencies through slow-motion and frame-by-frame visualization. Conclusion: Kinovea supports basic motion analysis by providing clear kinematic information and helping beginner athletes observe and refine their movement techniques. The findings also offer practical value for coaches by enabling more precise identification of inefficient patterns and guiding targeted corrections during early-stage training.
